process-compose and Overmind start several local processes, ordinary programs such as the parts of your app, on your computer from one file. Flisk does the same when every `service.json` has a `command`, with no [Docker](../start/words.md#docker), and can move to [containers](../start/words.md#container) later.

| | process-compose | Overmind | Flisk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Config file | `process-compose.yaml` | `Procfile` | `service.json` per service |
| Health-checked startup order | Yes (readiness probes) | No | Yes (`dependsOn` waits for `/health`) |
| Restart a crashed process | Yes (restart policies) | Partial (`--auto-restart`) | Yes (with backoff) |
| Prefixed, colored logs | Yes | Yes (tmux) | Yes |
| Terminal UI for the processes | Yes | Yes (tmux panes) | Not yet for local processes |
| Grow into containers with a database and gateway | No | No | Yes (drop `command` to use the Docker path) |

**Where they are stronger**

- **process-compose** has a richer TUI (a screen you can use inside the terminal) and more process options today.
- **Overmind** is tiny and works with any existing Procfile (a simple file that lists the command that starts each part).

More: [run-without-docker.md](../run-without-docker.md)

Cells describe each tool's own features as documented; "Partial" means it needs extra setup or covers part of the row. Spotted a mistake? [Open an issue](https://github.com/flisk-sh/flisk/issues/new).
